summary:
Bold Pear is a digital platform developed using Flutter and Dart, with support from Google Antigravity and Claude AI during development and Leonardo AI for visual design, to monitor and promote astronauts' mental health during space missions.

The project addresses psychological risks associated with isolation, confinement, distance from Earth, and other extreme conditions of space environments. Grounded in scientific research and official NASA studies, it uses validated PHQ-9 and GAD-7 questionnaires to monitor symptoms of depression and anxiety through periodic assessments lasting approximately five minutes.

Results are displayed in progress charts, helping astronauts identify emotional changes and receive personalized preventive guidance, including self-care practices and recommendations to seek professional assistance when necessary.

Featuring a human-centered, accessible, and multilingual interface, Bold Pear aims to provide astronauts with greater autonomy, complement specialized psychological care, and reduce dependence on real-time communication with Earth, contributing to crew well-being during long-duration space missions.
details:
Bold Pear — Intelligent Mental Health Monitoring for Astronauts

Project Overview

Bold Pear is a digital mental health monitoring platform designed for astronauts. Its purpose is to promote psychological well-being, identify early signs of emotional distress, and provide preventive guidance during space missions.

The project was developed to address one of the major challenges of space exploration: preserving astronauts' mental health in extreme environments characterized by prolonged isolation, confinement, radiation exposure, altered gravity, hostile environments, and distance from Earth.

These conditions can lead to psychological consequences, affecting astronauts' emotional health, mood, adaptability, and quality of life during space missions.

Our solution aims to transform periodic psychological assessments into a continuous, accessible, visual, and digital process, allowing astronauts to monitor their emotional well-being over time and receive appropriate guidance based on identified symptoms.

How Does It Work?

Bold Pear operates through periodic check-ins lasting approximately five minutes, during which astronauts complete scientifically grounded questionnaires.

The platform uses psychological screening instruments recognized in scientific literature, including:

  • PHQ-9 (Patient Health Questionnaire-9): An instrument used to identify and monitor the severity of depressive symptoms.
  • GAD-7 (Generalized Anxiety Disorder-7): An instrument used to assess the severity of anxiety symptoms.

The research also considers the Karolinska Sleepiness Scale (KSS) as a scientific reference for a potential future expansion of sleepiness and alertness monitoring.

After completing the questionnaires, the system calculates scores, displays symptom severity indicators, and records the results in historical charts, allowing users to visualize changes over time.

Based on the results, the platform provides self-care guidance and practices, such as guided breathing exercises, sleep schedule management, enjoyable activities, and strategies for managing worries.

When more severe symptoms or responses indicating possible self-harm are identified, the platform prioritizes guidance encouraging astronauts to immediately contact the crew's medical officer or a trusted crew member.

Bold Pear was designed to complement, rather than replace, professional psychological and psychiatric care. Its goal is to reduce the need for video calls solely for routine check-ins by providing structured monitoring between clinical assessments and facilitating the identification of situations requiring specialized attention.

Scientific Foundation

The development of Bold Pear was based on research involving psychological assessment instruments, the Measurement-Based Care (MBC) approach, and official NASA studies addressing behavioral health risks during space missions.

MBC uses standardized and repeated assessments to monitor symptoms and support clinical decision-making, rather than relying exclusively on occasional observations.

The scientific references considered include:

  • Kroenke, Spitzer, and Williams (2001): A study examining the validity of the PHQ-9 for assessing depressive symptom severity.
  • Spitzer et al. (2006): Research investigating the reliability and validity of the GAD-7 for assessing anxiety symptoms.
  • Santos et al. (2013): A Brazilian study examining the sensitivity and specificity of the PHQ-9.
  • Moreno et al. (2016): An investigation into the psychometric properties of the Brazilian Portuguese version of the GAD-7.
  • Kaida et al. (2006): Validation of the Karolinska Sleepiness Scale against behavioral and electroencephalographic indicators.
  • Aboraya et al. (2018): A review of measurement-based psychiatric care and its benefits for clinical monitoring.
  • NASA — Human System Risk Board (2025): The official document Risk of Adverse Cognitive or Behavioral Changes and Psychiatric Disorders Leading to In-mission Health and Performance and Long-term Health Effects (Behavioral Health Risk — Revision D.1), which examines behavioral health risks during space missions. The report identifies factors such as isolation, confinement, radiation, altered gravity, and distance from Earth, emphasizing the need to develop continuous monitoring tools, early risk detection methods, and preventive measures that reduce dependence on real-time communication with healthcare professionals on Earth.

These studies support the selection of assessment instruments and the use of repeated evaluations over time. However, the specific application of Bold Pear to astronauts still requires its own scientific validation.

Problems We Aim to Solve

Our team focused the development of Bold Pear on the psychological consequences (Psy) associated with stressors experienced during space missions.

Psychological Consequences (Psy)

Psychological consequences are related to astronauts' emotional health and include mood changes, symptoms of anxiety and depression, stress, and emotional distress.

These effects may arise or intensify due to factors characteristic of space missions, such as social isolation, prolonged confinement, separation from family members, excessive workload, and communication limitations with Earth.

In addition to identifying symptoms, this dimension also considers positive aspects of mental health, such as adaptability, coping strategies, and resilience.

Bold Pear directly addresses the monitoring of psychological indicators by using scientifically grounded questionnaires to track anxiety and depressive symptoms over time.

Through visual representations of results and preventive guidance, the platform aims to encourage self-care, facilitate early recognition of emotional changes, and guide astronauts on when to seek professional support.

Benefits and Expected Impact

The main benefit of Bold Pear is to provide a preventive monitoring tool that facilitates the early identification of emotional changes before they become more severe.

The platform aims to:

  • Promote greater autonomy and awareness of personal mental health.
  • Facilitate the identification of changes in anxiety and depressive symptoms.
  • Provide visual historical records to help identify individual trends and changes.
  • Offer simple self-care strategies adapted to the mission's daily routine.
  • Support the identification of situations requiring professional evaluation.
  • Complement remote psychological care and optimize the use of communication resources.
  • Contribute to crew resilience, emotional well-being, and quality of life.

During long-duration space missions, particularly future journeys to the Moon and Mars, communication with Earth may experience limitations and delays. In this context, digital monitoring and guidance solutions can contribute to greater crew autonomy while respecting medical and safety protocols.

The intended impact is to help preserve astronauts' mental health, contributing to a healthier emotional environment and the long-term sustainability of space exploration missions.

Creativity and Innovation

Bold Pear's key innovation lies in combining scientific foundations, longitudinal monitoring, prevention, and a human-centered interactive experience.

Instead of presenting psychological assessments as isolated clinical forms, the platform features a friendly virtual character, Bold Pear, who accompanies astronauts throughout their experience.

Its welcoming communication style and visual elements make the process more accessible and less intimidating, encouraging regular participation in psychological check-ins.

Another distinctive feature is the transformation of questionnaire responses into progress charts, allowing users to visually understand changes in their mental health indicators.

The system also provides multilingual support, including English, Portuguese, German, French, and Japanese, aiming to accommodate international crews.

The proposal combines structured monitoring and practical guidance within an interface designed for quick, intuitive, and recurring use.

Factors Considered During Development

During the design and development of Bold Pear, our team considered the following factors:

  • Extreme conditions of the space environment: Isolation, confinement, altered gravity, radiation, enclosed environments, and distance from Earth.
  • Scientific foundation: Selection of psychological instruments studied and validated across different populations.
  • Usability: Short assessments designed to minimize astronauts' workload.
  • Accessibility and inclusion: An intuitive interface, clear communication, and support for multiple languages.
  • Continuous monitoring: Comparison of results over time rather than relying exclusively on isolated assessments.
  • Psychological safety: Identification of responses requiring immediate attention and guidance to seek human support.
  • Autonomy: Availability of self-care practices without requiring a video conference for every routine recommendation.
  • Ethics and privacy: The need to protect sensitive information and restrict access to authorized individuals.
  • Clinical limitations: Recognition that screening instruments do not replace diagnoses, medical evaluations, or emergency protocols.

Technologies Used

Bold Pear was developed using Google Antigravity as the development environment, together with the Flutter framework and the Dart programming language, enabling the creation of a multiplatform application with a responsive, interactive, and user-friendly interface.

Artificial intelligence tools were also incorporated into the development process. Claude AI (Anthropic) supported programming, code development, problem-solving, and the organization of technical solutions, while Leonardo AI was used to create visual assets and contribute to the project's visual identity, including the friendly Bold Pear character.

Development included the implementation of scientifically grounded psychological questionnaires, response processing, score classification according to the PHQ-9 and GAD-7 scales, and visualization of mental health trends through interactive charts.

The application also incorporates accessibility features, multilingual support, and a human-centered interface represented by the Bold Pear character, who accompanies astronauts throughout their assessments and provides self-care guidance based on their results.

The combination of these technologies, alongside AI-assisted development and creative design tools, enabled the creation of an intuitive and engaging digital solution focused on preventive mental health monitoring in space environments.

Conclusion

Bold Pear proposes a more preventive, accessible, and human-centered approach to mental health monitoring during space exploration.

By integrating scientific assessment instruments, continuous monitoring, data visualization, and self-care guidance, we aim to provide astronauts with a tool that helps them recognize emotional changes, track their progress, and identify when specialized assistance is needed.

Our mission is to help ensure that, as humanity explores new worlds, the mental health of those who make that exploration possible remains a priority.
